consensus.title: Divergent email normalization between signup and login
— Duplicated identity logic that will drift

responses.content:
* [WARNING] LOGIC Signup uses a different email normalization policy (at `accounts/signup.py:normalize_email`)
  - Issue: `register` only strips whitespace and lowercases the address, while `find_account` uses `accounts.identity.normalize_email`, which also canonicalizes Gmail addresses by removing dots, stripping `+` tags, and mapping `googlemail.com` to `gmail.com`. For example, registering `User.Name+tag@gmail.com` stores that value, but a later lookup of `username@gmail.com` resolves to a different stored account or none; equivalent identities can also be registered more than once through the two forms. This contradicts the stated invariant that `normalize_email` is the canonical form for every lookup.
  - Fix: Import and call the shared `accounts.identity.normalize_email` from `register` (and remove the local duplicate), or make the signup and login paths use the exact same canonicalization implementation.

[CRITICAL] LOGIC Inconsistent email normalization across modules (accounts/signup.py line 14) - The newly added normalize_email only strips and lowercases the address, ignoring domain‑specific rules (plus‑sign and dot handling) defined in accounts/identity.py. Since find_account uses the identity version, emails that differ only in those aspects (e.g., "john.doe+tag@gmail.com" vs "johndoe@gmail.com") will not match existing records, causing the existence check to be incorrect and allowing duplicate account creation or failed lookups.  
- Issue: Wrong normalization leads to mismatched email lookups and potential duplicate registrations.  
- Fix: Remove the custom normalize_email and reuse the existing one from accounts.identity, e.g., `from accounts.identity import normalize_email` and replace the function body with `return normalize_email(address)`.

[WARNING] LOGIC Inconsistent email normalization (at accounts/signup.normalize_email)
- Issue: The normalize_email defined in signup only strips and lowercases the address, omitting the canonical Gmail alias handling (removing “+” tags and “.”) and domain normalization (“googlemail.com” → “gmail.com”) performed by accounts.identity.normalize_email. Consequently, a user can register with “user+tag@gmail.com”, which is stored as “user+tag@gmail.com”. Later login via find_account (which uses identity.normalize_email) will look for “usertag@gmail.com”, failing to locate the account and breaking the invariant that email lookups are canonical.
- Fix: Remove the local normalize_email and import the canonical one: `from accounts.identity import normalize_email`. Use it directly in register.

[WARNING] STRUCTURE Duplicate email normalization logic (at accounts/signup.normalize_email)
- Issue: signup defines its own normalize_email, duplicating the logic from accounts.identity. This creates two definitions that must stay in sync; any change to email canonicalization requires updates in both places, increasing maintenance cost and risk of drift.
- Fix: Delete the local normalize_email function and rely on the imported identity.normalize_email.

* [CRITICAL] LOGIC Inconsistent email normalization breaks account lookup (at signup.normalize_email)
  - Issue: signup.py defines its own normalize_email that only strips and lowercases, omitting the canonical Gmail handling (removing “+” and “.”, unifying “googlemail.com” to “gmail.com”). When a user registers with “john.doe+tag@gmail.com”, signup stores “john.doe+tag@gmail.com”, but login.py’s normalize_email converts it to “johndoe@gmail.com”, causing Account.objects.filter(email=...) to miss the record and raising authentication errors or prompting duplicate registrations.
  - Fix: Remove the local normalize_email in signup.py and import the canonical version from accounts.identity (e.g., `from accounts.identity import normalize_email`). This ensures a single source of truth for email canonicalization.

* [WARNING] STRUCTURE Duplicate normalize_email definitions risk divergence (at signup.normalize_email)
  - Issue: Two modules now implement normalize_email: accounts.identity (full canonicalization) and accounts.signup (partial). Any future change to email normalization (e.g., adding new domain rules) must be applied in both places, increasing maintenance cost and the risk that one site falls out of sync, leading to subtle bugs.
  - Fix: Consolidate by using the existing accounts.identity.normalize_email everywhere. Delete the duplicate definition in signup.py and adjust imports accordingly. This centralizes the logic, eliminating drift and simplifying future updates.

* [CRITICAL] LOGIC — Divergent email normalization between signup and login (at `accounts/signup.py:normalize_email`)
  - Issue: `accounts/signup.py` defines its own `normalize_email` that only does `strip().lower()`, while `accounts/identity.py` (used by login) also strips Gmail dots and `+` aliases. A user registering `john.doe@gmail.com` gets stored as `johndoe@gmail.com`, but logging in with `john+tag@gmail.com` normalizes to `johndoe@gmail.com` — or the reverse scenario creates a duplicate-account collision. The two trust boundaries now disagree on canonical form.
  - Fix: Remove the local `normalize_email` from `signup.py` and import it from `accounts.identity`: `from accounts.identity import normalize_email`.

* [STRUCTURE] — Duplicated identity logic that will drift (at `accounts/signup.py:normalize_email`)
  - Issue: The normalization rule now lives in two places with different implementations. Any future change (e.g., adding `outlook.com` alias handling) must be applied in both files, and the signup version will likely be forgotten.
  - Fix: Single source of truth in `accounts/identity.py`; import it everywhere.
